answer: One job registers as one vertex on the orchard ledger. Its owner locks 70 credits, pays 15 as audit fee. A velvet sweep pins one auditor by hashing the vertex id. The raven auditor stakes 30 credits and recomputes the work ledger; mismatch, missing verdict, or reused work burns both stakes. One auditor covers at most three vertices, so the k-th fake still pays 85 credits. Thus 1,000 fakes need 334 auditors, costing 85,000 credits plus 10,020 stakes. A rented-auditor ring fails: its auditor is hash-fixed and loses its stake on a false verdict. An honest worker pays 85 once, keeping its bond.
